MAGNIFICENT MONSTERA · four comps · 18 × 24 in

One leaf drawing is shared across all four, so the directions differ on register — ink, frame, voice — rather than on draughtsmanship. Copy is real botany: Araceae, southern Mexico to Panama, hemiepiphyte, costilla de Adán / piñanona. Anything in [brackets] is a placeholder for you to fill in — edition size, paper, plate number.

Type here is Space Grotesk / Archivo Black / Instrument Serif / Bricolage Grotesque standing in for Apercu, which can't load in this environment.

A · KAPPAZURI — the studio's own base register: two inks and one spark, stencil-flat, with a deliberate off-register pull and a halftone screen under the type.

Why: it looks like Essentials Creative and like nothing else on the wall. Cheapest to print — two spot inks — and the strongest of the four in grayscale.

Tradeoff: the quietest at a distance, and it asks the leaf to carry the whole poster alone.

B · RHIZO LAND — the devotional frame from the Rhizomatic border system: zigzag band, agave mat, Yokoo ray field, bilingual cartouches top and bottom.

Why: reads immediately as community work, and it is the only direction that puts Spanish first.

Tradeoff: the frame competes with the leaf for attention, and the ray field is a great deal of ink on paper.

C · RHIZO WATER — a botanical plate, submerged. The only direction carrying the real information: family, range, habit, names.

Why: it earns time up close, and it reads as a series — "Plate [__]" implies more leaves to come.

Tradeoff: a full-bleed indigo ground drinks ink and shows every handling mark, and it is the weakest across a room.

D · KIRA KIRA — the prismatic register: the leaf as a light-refracting form on a pearl ground.

Why: the outlier, and the one most likely to travel well on a phone screen.

Tradeoff: farthest from the studio's usual voice, and flat-ink printing will not hold that gradient — this one wants foil or a digital press.
